data.decision: Committed files carry generic project policy only. Reviewer endpoints, model names of a private deployment, API-key variables, LAN hosts/IPs, and machine-specific sizing (test worker counts) go in git-ignored local files: .ddflow/reviewers.toml, .ddflow/gates.toml (later .ddflow/local/config.toml), an untracked .roborev.toml, .claude/settings.local.json. Task bodies, research records, lessons and commit messages refer to such a service by role ('the LAN critic, see local config'), never by address. ddflow RECOMMENDS services to a new user; it never ships one person's configuration. History is not rewritten (operator, 2026-09-29).
data.title: Nobody's own services are committed: endpoints, hosts, keys and machine sizing live in git-ignored local files

data.body:
Operator 2026-09-29: 'make sure the critic llm configs, the roborev configs, and all companions configs are local for this project and are not pushed to the git repo, as we want to keep the repo and the mcp server/ddflow tool generic ... This tool should only recommend to a new agent or user, but not provide him a configuration which is customized for my setup - as LLM IP addresses, keys, etc. My own critic / roborev configs should stay local per this project'. Audit of tracked files: .ddflow/config.toml carries [[reviewer]] base_url http://10.220.230.8:8000/v1 and a unit_tests command sized to this 192-core machine (-n 48); .roborev.toml carries agent='kilo' and comments naming the LAN DeepSeek (10.220.230.242) and Qwen (10.220.230.8) hosts; .claude/settings.json carries the SessionStart hook with /home/delian/src/ddflow absolute paths. No real keys are tracked (only test dummies); the Kilo key lives in ~/.config/ddflow/kilo.key. ddflow has NO local layer today: Config.load reads only .ddflow/config.toml, and tomlcfg.config_paths (reviewers/companions/gates/macros) only .ddflow/<file>. (a) .ddflow/local/config.toml (local/ is already gitignored) is read LAST: by Config.load (source 'local' in config --explain) and by config_paths for every [[reviewer]]/[[companion]]/[gate.*]/[[macro]] overlay; (b) this repo: [[reviewer]] and the -n 48 command move to .ddflow/local/config.toml, the committed config keeps a generic '-n auto' and no reviewer; .roborev.toml untracked + ignored, .roborev.toml.example committed with the generic review guidelines and no agent/host; the Claude hook moves to .claude/settings.local.json (ignored) and ddflow's claude hook installer writes there because it embeds absolute paths. Tests: a local reviewer/gate/knob overrides the committed one and is reported as 'local'; hooks install --claude writes settings.local.json. History: the LAN addresses are in already-pushed history (20d0073 onward) -- rewriting it is the operator's call, not done here.

No new code paths: reuses tomlcfg.config_paths' existing reviewers.toml/gates.toml overlay instead of a new mechanism; the guard is the only private-address scan in the suite (gitleaks config covers secrets, not hosts).

data.summary: tests/test_repo_is_generic.py guard has four holes (LAN critic, CONFIRMED by reading): an address ending a sentence ('at 10.220.1.8.') is not matched (trailing (?![\d.])); the .roborev.toml exemption is a prefix so .roborev.toml.example is skipped; the 10.0.0.5 fixture exemption applies in every file, not only tests/test_container.py; private IPv6 (fc00::/7, fe80::/10) is not checked at all.
